This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.\nDaisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"\nAssistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.\nDaisy: "Please review PR #1234"\nAssistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example>\n\n<example>\nContext: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.\nDaisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"\nAssistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."\n<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>\n</example> (Tools: All tools)
- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)
- vercel:ai-architect: Specializes in architecting AI-powered applications on Vercel — choosing between AI SDK patterns, configuring providers, building agents, setting up durable workflows, and integrating MCP servers. Use when designing AI features, building chatbots, or creating agentic applications. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)
- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)
- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)
- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Agent)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.
</system-reminder>

## Auto Mode Active

Bias toward working without stopping for clarifying questions — when you'd normally pause to check, make the reasonable call and keep going; they'll redirect you if needed. If the user, a skill, or the shape of the task suggests they want you to ask (with AskUserQuestion or otherwise), do so. 1	import React, { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
2	import type { RefObject } from 'react';
3	import { useDisclosure } from '@chakra-ui/react';
4	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
5	import logger from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/logger-instance';
6	import { CartDrawerContainer } from 'app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer';
7	
8	/*
9	 * SFCC-11 plan step 9 (final commit) — mirrors the shape of base's own
10	 * `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` (a state-builder hook + a Context Provider + a Context-reading
11	 * hook), but simpler in one real, verified way: unlike base's modal, this drawer takes no
12	 * "item added" payload at all — across all 17 Figma state groups there is no "just added" state,
13	 * the drawer always renders whatever the current basket contains (see `CartDrawerContainer`'s own
14	 * docblock). So the shared state here is just isOpen/onOpen/onClose, and Chakra's own
15	 * `useDisclosure()` — already used for exactly this shape elsewhere in this codebase
16	 * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:126`) — is the more idiomatic choice than hand-rolling base's raw
17	 * `useState`.
18	 *
19	 * Two real constraints shaped this file, both found by reading the actual current code rather
20	 * than assumed:
21	 *
22	 * 1. **The structural trap base's own code fell into.** `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in
23	 *    base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or
24	 *    override (confirmed by grepping the whole `retail-react-app` package) — a component can't
25	 *    easily be both a Context's wrapper and a Context's consumer of its own child in the same
26	 *    render pass, and base's own code never solved that, so add-to-cart has shipped with zero
27	 *    visual feedback. Fixed here by making `CartDrawerProvider` itself render
28	 *    `CartDrawerContainer` (the file that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket
29	 *    content) — the Provider can never be mounted without the real UI being fed real props,
30	 *    because both happen in the same component body.
31	 *
32	 * 2. **`_app` needs this same live state for its own bag-icon click handler, and `_app` is the
33	 *    component that mounts `CartDrawerProvider`.** A component cannot consume a context it is
34	 *    itself providing within its own subtree — there is no ancestor `CartDrawerProvider` above
35	 *    `_app`'s own top-level code, only a descendant one it's about to render. `useCartDrawerState`
36	 *    is exported separately from `useCartDrawer` so `_app` can call the *raw* state builder
37	 *    directly (the same way it already calls plain `useDisclosure()` directly for its own mobile
38	 *    nav drawer state) and pass the resulting value into `<CartDrawerProvider value={...}>` —
39	 *    so `_app`'s own handler and every nested consumer (`product-view`) always observe the
40	 *    identical live state, never two independent copies. `useCartDrawer()` (the Context reader)
41	 *    is for every other consumer, which — unlike `_app` — genuinely is a descendant of the
42	 *    Provider.
43	 */
44	
45	export type CartDrawerContextValue = {
46	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
47	  isOpen: boolean;
48	  /**
49	   * Opens the drawer. Pass the element that should receive focus back once the drawer closes
50	   * (AC10) — e.g. the real clicked `<button>`/`<IconButton>` DOM node. Mirrors
51	   * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `handleTriggerClick` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:267-276`):
52	   * capture a real element at the moment of the triggering interaction, rather than reading
53	   * `document.activeElement` later — that file's own comment on why
54	   * (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:268-269`) applies identically here: a mouse click does not
55	   * reliably focus the clicked element in every browser. Omit/pass `null`/`undefined` when no
56	   * trigger element is available; the previous trigger (if any) is left untouched rather than
57	   * cleared, so a best-effort focus target is still preferred over none.
58	   */
59	  onOpen: (trigger?: HTMLElement | null) => void;
60	  /** Closes the drawer. Does not clear `triggerRef` — see `handleCloseComplete` in
61	   *  `zimmDrawer/index.tsx`, which reads `finalFocusRef` only after the close animation
62	   *  finishes, i.e. strictly after `onClose` has already run. Clearing the ref here would
63	   *  make AC10 focus-return silently fail on every close. */
64	  onClose: () => void;
65	  /** AC10 focus-return target — whichever element was last passed to `onOpen`. Forward to
66	   *  `ZimmDrawer`/`CartDrawerContainer`'s `finalFocusRef` prop. Typed as `RefObject<HTMLElement>`
67	   *  (not `| null`) to satisfy that prop's own type — same typing precedent as
68	   *  `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `triggerRef` (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:88,140`). */
69	  triggerRef: RefObject<HTMLElement>;
70	};
71	
72	// Exported (not just used internally) for the same reason base exports `AddToCartModalContext`
73	// directly (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:59`) — lets a test wrap a subtree with a controlled value
74	// via `CartDrawerContext.Provider` directly, without going through the real state builder.
75	export const CartDrawerContext = createContext<CartDrawerContextValue | undefined>(undefined);
76	
77	/**
78	 * Builds the cart drawer's shared isOpen/onOpen/onClose state plus its AC10 focus-return
79	 * trigger ref — the raw equivalent of base's own `useAddToCartModal()`. Called exactly once, by
80	 * `_app`, which passes the result into `CartDrawerProvider`'s `value` prop — see this file's own
81	 * module docblock (constraint 2) for why `_app` needs the raw builder rather than
82	 * `useCartDrawer()`'s Context read.
83	 *
84	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
85	 */
86	export const useCartDrawerState = (): CartDrawerContextValue => {
87	  const { isOpen, onOpen: onDisclosureOpen, onClose } = useDisclosure();
88	  // Typed as HTMLElement (not HTMLElement | null) so `.current` is writable below — same cast
89	  // and reasoning as useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:140 (a plain `useRef<HTMLElement>(null)` would
90	  // infer the read-only `RefObject<HTMLElement>` overload instead of `MutableRefObject`).
91	  const triggerRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null as unknown as HTMLElement);
92	
93	  const onOpen = (trigger?: HTMLElement | null): void => {
94	    if (trigger) triggerRef.current = trigger;
95	    onDisclosureOpen();
96	  };
97	
98	  // Judgement call (no AC or Figma state describes this either way — see this hook's own
99	  // module docblock and the PR report for the fuller reasoning): close the drawer whenever the
100	  // route changes, mirroring base `use-add-to-cart-modal.js`'s own `[pathname]`-keyed effect
101	  // (`use-add-to-cart-modal.js:603-611`) and this exact file's sibling precedent —
102	  // `_app/index.tsx`'s own mobile-nav drawer already closes itself the same way
103	  // (`_app/index.tsx`'s own `useEffect(() => { onClose(); }, [location])`, "Lets automatically
104	  // close the mobile navigation when the location path is changed."). Concretely load-bearing,
105	  // not just consistency: `ZimmCartButtonGroup`'s Checkout button (already built, SFCC-275)
106	  // navigates via a plain `history.push('/checkout')` with no `onClose` call of its own
107	  // (verified directly against `zimmCartButtonGroup/index.tsx`'s `handleCheckoutClick`), and
108	  // `ZimmDrawer`'s overlay is not click-through — without this effect, clicking Checkout from
109	  // inside the cart drawer would navigate to `/checkout` while the drawer stayed open on top of
110	  // it, leaving the shopper unable to see or reach the page they just navigated to.
111	  const { pathname } = useLocation();
112	  useEffect(() => {
113	    if (isOpen) {
114	      onClose();
115	    }
116	    // Deliberately keyed on pathname alone, matching use-add-to-cart-modal.js's own shape —
117	    // isOpen/onClose are read for their current value, not to decide when the effect re-runs.
118	  }, [pathname]);
119	
120	  return { isOpen, onOpen, onClose, triggerRef };
121	};
122	
123	// Stable (module-level, not per-render) no-op fallback for when no CartDrawerProvider is
124	// mounted above the caller — see useCartDrawer's own doc for why this degrades instead of
125	// throwing. `triggerRef` is a plain inert object, not a real useRef() result: nothing outside a
126	// real CartDrawerProvider subtree ever reads it back for a real focus call.
127	const FALLBACK_ONLY: CartDrawerContextValue = {
128	  isOpen: false,
129	  onOpen: () => {
130	    // A real shopper's page always has a CartDrawerProvider ancestor (mounted once in `_app`),
131	    // so reaching this in a real request is a genuine bug, not an expected path — logged so a
132	    // silently-broken Add to Bag button is at least observable, rather than a shopper clicking
133	    // it and nothing happening with no trace anywhere.
134	    logger.warn('useCartDrawer called with no CartDrawerProvider mounted — Add to Bag will not open the cart drawer.', {
135	      namespace: 'useCartDrawer',
136	    });
137	  },
138	  onClose: () => undefined,
139	  triggerRef: { current: null },
140	};
141	
142	/**
143	 * Reads the shared cart-drawer state from Context. For any consumer that is a genuine descendant
144	 * of `CartDrawerProvider` (e.g. `product-view`) — see this file's own module docblock for why
145	 * `_app` itself must use `useCartDrawerState()` directly instead.
146	 *
147	 * Degrades to a stable, harmless no-op outside a Provider — the same shape `useUiCopy.ts` already
148	 * uses (`useContext(...) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY`) — rather than throwing. Confirmed necessary, not
149	 * merely convenient: `product-view/index.stories.tsx` (unmodified by this change — not in this
150	 * step's own manifest) wraps `ProductView`'s stories in the now-removed `AddToCartModalProvider`,
151	 * with no `CartDrawerProvider` in its own decorator stack, and every one of its stories renders
152	 * the real default `ProductView` export, which calls this hook unconditionally near its own top
153	 * level. A throwing `useCartDrawer` (this file's own first draft, matching `useIntl`'s
154	 * load-bearing/non-degrading precedent) crashes all four of that file's stories on mount, before
155	 * any interaction — verified live against a real running Storybook instance, not assumed (see
156	 * this step's own PR report). `onOpen`'s own no-op additionally logs a warning (see
157	 * `FALLBACK_ONLY` above) so a genuine missing-Provider bug in the real app — which should never
158	 * happen, since `_app` always mounts one — is still observable rather than a silent dead button.
159	 *
160	 * @returns The shared cart-drawer state — see `CartDrawerContextValue`.
161	 */
162	export const useCartDrawer = (): CartDrawerContextValue => useContext(CartDrawerContext) ?? FALLBACK_ONLY;
163	
164	export type CartDrawerProviderProps = {
165	  /** The live state to provide — built via `useCartDrawerState()` by the one caller (`_app`)
166	   *  that also needs it directly for its own bag-icon click handler. Accepting it as a prop
167	   *  (rather than calling `useCartDrawerState()` internally) is what lets `_app` and every
168	   *  nested consumer share the exact same instance — see this file's own module docblock,
169	   *  constraint 2. */
170	  value: CartDrawerContextValue;
171	  children: React.ReactNode;
172	};
173	
174	/**
175	 * Provides the shared cart-drawer state to `children` AND renders `CartDrawerContainer` — the
176	 * component that actually renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` with real basket content — in the same
177	 * place. See this file's own module docblock, constraint 1, for why both happen together here
178	 * rather than leaving `CartDrawerContainer` for some other, easily-forgotten call site to mount.
179	 *
180	 * Written with `React.createElement` rather than JSX so this file can stay `.ts` (as named in
181	 * the SFCC-11 plan's own file manifest) — every other source file under `overrides/app/hooks/`
182	 * is `.ts` with no JSX in it; `useUiCopy.ts`'s own Provider is a separate `.tsx` component under
183	 * `overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/` rather than living in the hook file itself, which
184	 * is the established split this codebase already uses for exactly this shape. Splitting
185	 * `CartDrawerProvider` out the same way was the more consistent option but would have meant
186	 * creating a file outside this step's own manifest — flagged in the PR report, not decided
187	 * silently. `React.createElement(...)` has one direct precedent already in this codebase for
188	 * the identical reason (a `.ts` file needing to produce a React element without JSX syntax):
189	 * `overrides/app/components/forms/useAddressFields.test.ts:26`.
190	 */
191	export const CartDrawerProvider = ({ value, children }: CartDrawerProviderProps): React.ReactElement =>
192	  React.createElement(
193	    CartDrawerContext.Provider,
194	    { value },
195	    children,
196	    React.createElement(CartDrawerContainer, {
197	      isOpen: value.isOpen,
198	      onClose: value.onClose,
199	      finalFocusRef: value.triggerRef,
200	    }),
201	  );
